points.text: Shuaib (a.s) is also knows as Jethro in biblical history. He was sent to the people of Madyan which is modern day Jordan and near to the Red Sea. The people were also known as Ashab al Aiykah or the Companions of the Wood as they used to worship a large tree.

The people of Madyan practiced many things prohibited including idolatry, collecting interest, cheating customers in business transaction and were involved in robbery and attacking travelers who passed by their towns to take over their possessions and wealth.

When the azaab (or scourge) came upon the people of Madyan, it started with unbearable hot weather. The next day, a huge black cloud filled the sky. Seeing this the people thought it would be the end of the scorching heat. The disbelievers gathered under the cloud, hoping it would bring refreshing and cool rain. But a huge thunderstorm fell over them followed by a severe earthquake that ended the lives of all the disbelievers of Madyan.

When Shuaib (a.s) and his followers returned to Madyan, they were shocked to see the fate of the disbelievers. However, they did not feel any regret as Shuaib (a.s) had already fulfilled his duty to warn the people of Madyan but they chose not to listen.
Shuaib (a.s) had two daughters. One of them (it is believed her name was Safura), got married to prophet Musa (a.s) when Musa took refuge in Madyan, while running away from the Egyptians.

verses.text: To the People of Madyan, their brother Shuaib a.s was sent. The people were unjust in their measure and weight, and would ambush people traveling on the roads. (Surah Al-A’raf : Section 11)

The leaders who disbelieved from among his people said: “If you follow Shuaib, you shall indeed be losers!”. Thereupon an earthquake overtook them and they became lifeless bodies in their homes with their faces down. (Surah Al-A’raf : Section 11)
Those who called Shuaib a liar were as though they never lived therein; those who called Shuaib a liar were the actual losers. (Surah Al-A’raf : Section 11)
To the people of Madyan, Allah sent their brother Shuaib (a.s). (Surah Hud : Section 8)
The people were prone to giving short measure and weight. Shuaib (a.s) warned against this and conveyed the message to worship one God. (Surah Hud : Section 8)
The people argued that they will not give up their ways nor the deities whom their forefathers worshipped. (Surah Hud : Section 8)

Shuaib (a.s) further warned them saying : “O my people! Let not my dispute with you bring upon you the doom similar to that of the people of Nuh or of Hud or of Saleh, nor are the people of Lut far off from you”. (Surah Hud : Section 8)
But the people were bent upon disbelief and said that if it were not for Shuaib’s family, they would have certainly stoned him to death. (Surah Hud : Section 8)
Allah delivered Shuaib and those who believed through his special mercy. A mighty blast seized the wrongdoers and they lay dead in their homes, face down. (Surah Hud : Section 8)

The people of Aiykah also disbelieved the Rasools. Shuaib (a.s) warned them to fear Allah and not to give less in measure and to weigh with even scales. He warned them not to cheat your fellow men of what is rightfully theirs, and not to spread evil in the land. (Surah Ash-Shu’ara : Section 10)

The people said that he was surely bewitched and that he was no more than a human being like them. They called him a liar and asked that a fragment from the sky fall on them, if what he was saying was true. (Surah Ash-Shu’ara : Section 10)

The torment of the day of shadow (dark clouds carrying Allah’s scourge) seized them, and indeed, it was an extremely dreadful day. Surely in this story there is a great lesson, but most of these people do not learn and become believers. (Surah Ash-Shu’ara : Section 10)
The people of Madyan denied their brother Shuaib (a.s). So a severe earthquake seized them and they lay dead, prostrate in their dwellings. (Surah Al-Ankabut : Section 4)
